Thanks again for the call earlier — good to align. Per our discussion, attaching an initial sample of the prompts and a small set of anonymized system logs. This should give you a sense of variability and edge cases we care about (slot filling, multi-turn context, and domain-specific entities).

High-level asks from our side: 
- We want to evaluate latency at 95th pct for 512 tokens and accuracy on our intent extraction golden set (we'll share the mapping).
- Can you propose a minimal evaluation plan and success criteria?
- Timeline: we are hoping for a 2-week technical POC starting the week of Mar 22. Is that feasible?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - prompt/examples & logs

Sofia —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks on the call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

Recap of goals
- Primary: Validate inference quality on your intent extraction + slot-filling across multi-turn prompts.
- Secondary: Verify 95th-pct latency for 512-token responses and cost/run estimates for your expected throughput.

Proposed success criteria (draft)
- Quality: >= 92% F1 on your intent/slot golden set (we'll map labels).
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 350ms for 1 concurrent request baseline and <= 550ms at expected concurrency (you indicated ~20 qps peak).
- Stability: no service errors > 0.1% and KV-cache hit rate improvements for prefix reuse > 20% (if applicable).

Minimal evaluation plan
- Deliverables from Acme: prompt set CSV (you sent), golden-label mapping, expected traffic profile (samples/sec and concurrency), any redaction rules for logs.
- Deliverables from Redwood: eval harness + scripts, baseline runs on a chosen model variant, per-route dashboards, and a short report with recommended config (batching, quantization, routing).
- Timeline: start technical POC week of Mar 22, run 7 business days of evaluation, 3 business days for analysis & final report.

Owners
- Redwood PM/lead: Marissa Cole (poc coordination)
- Redwood SE: Aditya Rao (eval harness + infra)
- Acme lead: Sofia Ramos (data + label mapping)

Questions for you
1) Can you confirm the exact qps and concurrency expected during the POC window?
2) Are there any prompts in the sample that must be excluded from the eval (PII / regulatory)?
3) Do you have a preferred model family (open model) or should Aditya recommend based on the prompt distribution?

I cc'd Vivek for pricing/commitment questions but we can keep the POC minimal. Aditya will follow up with a short technical plan and infra checklist. If the timeline above works, we'll send a formal kickoff invite for Mon Mar 22.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acmeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - prompt/examples & logs

Hi Sofia — quick technical note / proposed eval steps from our side (keeps the POC focused and automatable):

1) Data prep:
- We'll ingest acme_prompt_sample.csv and apply the redaction rules you provide. We'll also sample additional context windows for multi-turn cases.

2) Model selection & baseline:
- Suggest we start with an Llama-2-13B-quant variant (low mem, good quality) and a higher-capacity 30B open model for comparison. If you have licensing constraints, let us know.

3) Metrics & harness:
- Intent/slot F1 (per-intent breakdown)
- Response latency distributions (p50/p90/p95) for 128/512 token scenarios
- Tokenization edge-case failures and hallucination spot checks (random sample of 200 responses)

4) Ownership & infra checklist:
- Aditya (Redwood SE) will provide a Dockerized eval harness and instructions to run in our hosted sandbox.
- Acme provides label mapping and concurrency profile (qps, burst patterns).

5) POC run plan + timeline:
- Mon Mar 22: infra sandbox ready + smoke test (1 day)
- Tue-Wed Mar 23-24: baseline runs and initial quality pass
- Thu-Fri Mar 25-26: load/latency runs and config iteration
- Mon Mar 29: deliverable report and recommended config

If this looks good I'll attach the harness README and the small infra checklist in a follow-up message.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acmeai.com>

Subject: Re: POC kickoff - prompt/examples & logs

Thanks Marissa and Aditya — that plan looks good. A few clarifications: 

- Concurrency: our target is 18 qps sustained with bursts up to 30 qps for short windows (30-60s).
- We flagged 6 rows in the sample CSV that contain PII; we'll send a redacted version by EOD today. Please exclude the unredacted file from any hub sharing.
- For models: no licensing constraints — prefer a balance of quality and cost, so the two-model comparison you suggested is ideal.

I'll share the redacted CSV and the golden-label mapping today. We can confirm the kickoff Mon morning — I can be online for a quick smoke test around 10:00 AM PT.

Attachments: acme_prompt_sample_redacted.csv, acme_golden_labels_v1.csv

Best,
Sofia
